211: Hill explains that between ages 30 and 40, people begin to learn the art of sex transmutation, usually unconsciously. They may observe that their powers of achievement have increased around 35 to 40, but most are unfamiliar with the cause—Nature begins to harmonize the emotions of love and sex between 30 and 40 so they may draw upon these great forces jointly. Sex alone is a mighty urge to action, but its forces are like a cyclone—often uncontrollable. When love begins to mix with sex, the result is calmness of purpose, poise, accuracy of judgment, and balance. When driven by desire to please based solely on sex, individuals may be capable of great achievement but their actions may be disorganized, distorted, and destructive—they may steal, cheat, even commit murder. But when LOVE is mixed with sex, the same individuals will guide actions with sanity, balance, and reason. Criminologists have discovered that hardened criminals can be reformed through the influence of strong love, but there is no record of reformation solely through sex. Reformation comes through the heart, not the head—a 'change of heart,' not a 'change of head.' Love, romance, and sex are all emotions capable of driving individuals to super-achievement. Love is the safety valve ensuring balance, poise, and constructive effort. When combined, these three emotions may lift one to the altitude of a genius.
212: Hill notes there are geniuses who know little of love—most may be found engaged in destructive action or action not based on justice and fairness. If good taste permitted, a dozen geniuses in industry and finance could be named who ride ruthlessly over others' rights, seemingly lacking conscience. The emotions are states of mind. Nature has provided a chemistry of the mind operating similarly to chemistry of matter—just as a chemist can create a deadly poison by mixing harmless elements, emotions may be combined to create a deadly poison. Sex and jealousy mixed may turn a person into an insane beast. The presence of destructive emotions creates a poison that may destroy one's sense of justice and fairness, and in extreme cases, destroy reason. The road to genius consists of the development, control, and proper use of sex, love, and romance—encouraging these as dominating thoughts while discouraging all destructive emotions. The mind is a creature of habit, thriving upon dominating thoughts fed to it. Through willpower, one may discourage any emotion and encourage any other. Control comes from persistence and habit. The secret of control lies in understanding transmutation—when a negative emotion presents itself, it can be transmuted into a constructive emotion by changing one's thoughts. THERE IS NO OTHER ROAD TO GENIUS THAN THROUGH VOLUNTARY SELF EFFORT! People may attain great heights by sex energy alone, but history shows they usually carry traits that rob them of the ability to keep or enjoy their fortune.
213: Hill discusses the emotion of love's enduring nature. Love brings out and develops the artistic and aesthetic nature, leaving its impress upon one's very soul even after the fire has been subdued. Memories of love never pass—they linger, guide, and influence long after the source of stimulation has faded. Every person moved by genuine love knows it leaves enduring traces upon the human heart. Love's effect endures because love is spiritual in nature. Individuals who cannot be stimulated to great heights by love are hopeless—dead, though they may seem to live. Even memories of love are sufficient to lift one to a higher plane of creative effort. Love's major force may spend itself and pass like a burned-out fire, but it leaves indelible marks, often preparing the heart for a still greater love. Hill advises going back into yesterdays and bathing the mind in beautiful memories of past love—it will soften present worries and annoyances, provide escape from unpleasant realities, and perhaps yield some idea or plan which may change the entire financial or spiritual status of your life. If you believe yourself unfortunate because you have loved and lost, perish the thought—one who has loved truly can never lose entirely. Love is whimsical and temperamental, coming when it pleases and going without warning. Accept and enjoy it while it remains, but spend no time worrying about its departure. Love may come and go times without number, but no two love experiences affect one in just the same way. All love experiences are beneficial except to the person who becomes resentful and cynical when love departs.
214: Hill distinguishes love from sex: love is spiritual while sex is biological. Love is chemistry; sex is physics. No experience touching the human heart with spiritual force can be harmful, except through ignorance or jealousy. Love is, without question, life's greatest experience—it brings one into communion with Infinite Intelligence. When mixed with romance and sex, it may lead one far up the ladder of creative effort. The emotions of love, sex, and romance are sides of the eternal triangle of achievement-building genius. Nature creates geniuses through no other force. Love has many sides, shades, and colors—the love for parents or children differs from love for one's sweetheart (one is mixed with sex, the other is not). Friendship love is another form, as is love of Nature's handiwork. But the most intense and burning of all is the blending of love and sex. Marriages not blessed with the eternal affinity of love and sex, properly balanced, cannot be fully happy and seldom endure. Love alone will not bring happiness in marriage, nor will sex alone. But when these two are blended, marriage may bring a state of mind closest to the spiritual one may know during earthly existence. When romance is added to love and sex, the obstructions between the finite human mind and Infinite Intelligence can be removed. Genius status can be attained. And The Tenth Step to Riches can be mastered.
215: This page features a single inspirational quote in large text: 'Positive and negative emotions cannot occupy the mind at the same time. ONE OR THE OTHER MUST DOMINATE.' This quote serves as a thematic divider between Chapter 10 (Sex Transmutation) and Chapter 11 (The Subconscious Mind), encapsulating a core principle: that the mind cannot simultaneously hold positive and negative emotions—one must prevail. The page bears the OceanofPDF.com watermark.
216: This page opens Chapter 11: THE SUBCONSCIOUS MIND—The Connecting Link (The Eleventh Step to Riches). Hill defines the subconscious mind as a field of consciousness where every impulse of thought or sensation reaching the objective mind through the five senses is classified and recorded, and from which thoughts may be recalled like letters from a filing cabinet. The subconscious receives and files sense impressions regardless of nature. One may VOLUNTARILY plant any plan, thought, or purpose desired for translation into physical or monetary equivalent. The subconscious acts first on dominating desires mixed with emotional feeling, such as FAITH. THE SUBCONSCIOUS MIND WORKS DAY AND NIGHT. Through a method not yet understood, it draws upon the forces of Infinite Intelligence for the power with which it voluntarily transmutes one's desires into their physical equivalent, making use always of the most practical media. Hill connects this to Chapter 1's six actions and Chapter 6's plan formulation, emphasizing the importance of understanding the subconscious's role.
217: Hill states that while one cannot entirely control the subconscious mind, one can voluntarily hand over any plan, desire, or purpose for transformation into concrete form. He references Chapter 3's instructions for using the subconscious. There is plenty of evidence that the subconscious is the connecting link between the finite human mind and Infinite Intelligence—the intermediary through which one may draw upon Infinite Intelligence at will. It alone contains the secret process by which mental impulses are modified into their spiritual equivalent. It alone is the medium through which prayer may be transmitted to the source capable of answering prayer. The possibilities of creative effort connected with the subconscious are stupendous and imponderable, inspiring awe. Hill confesses he never approaches this subject without feeling of littleness, due to our pitifully limited knowledge. After accepting the subconscious's reality and understanding its possibilities, one comprehends the full significance of Chapter 1's DESIRE instructions—why one was repeatedly admonished to MAKE DESIRES CLEAR AND REDUCE THEM TO WRITING, and the necessity of PERSISTENCE. The 13 Steps to Riches are the stimuli with which one acquires ability to reach and influence the subconscious. Do not become discouraged if you cannot do this upon first attempt—the subconscious may be voluntarily directed only through habit, using Chapter 2's FAITH directions. Be patient. Be persistent.
218: Hill explains that thoughts of fear, poverty, and all negative thoughts serve as stimuli to the subconscious mind—unless one masters these impulses and gives the subconscious more desirable food. The subconscious will not remain idle! If you fail to plant DESIRES, it will feed upon thoughts reaching it through neglect. Thought impulses, both negative and positive, reach the subconscious continuously from the four sources mentioned in Chapter 10. One is living daily amidst all manner of thought impulses reaching the subconscious without knowledge or awareness—some negative, some positive. The task is to help shut off the flow of negative impulses and voluntarily influence the subconscious through positive impulses of DESIRE. When achieved, one possesses the key unlocking the door to the subconscious, controlling it so completely that no undesirable thought can influence it. Everything human beings create BEGINS in the form of a thought impulse. Through the imagination, thought impulses may be assembled into plans. All thought impulses intended for transmutation and voluntarily planted in the subconscious must pass through the imagination and be mixed with faith. The mixing of faith with a plan or purpose for submission to the subconscious can be done ONLY through the imagination. The voluntary use of the subconscious calls for coordination and application of all the principles in this book. Hill quotes Ella Wheeler Wilcox: 'You never can tell what a thought will do / In bringing you hate or love— / For thoughts are things, and their airy wings / Are swifter than carrier doves.'
219: Hill continues quoting Ella Wheeler Wilcox's poem: 'They follow the law of the universe— / Each thing creates its kind, / And they speed o'er the track to bring you back / Whatever went out from your mind.' Mrs. Wilcox understood that thoughts going out from one's mind also embed themselves deeply in the subconscious, where they serve as a magnet, pattern, or blueprint by which the subconscious is influenced while translating them into physical equivalent. Thoughts are truly things because every material thing begins in the form of 'thought-energy.' The subconscious is more susceptible to influence by thought impulses mixed with feeling or emotion than by those originating solely in the reasoning portion of the mind. There is much evidence supporting the theory that ONLY emotionalized thoughts have any ACTION influence upon the subconscious. Emotion or feeling rules the majority of people. If the subconscious responds more quickly to emotionalized thought impulses, it is essential to become familiar with the more important emotions. There are seven major positive emotions and seven major negative emotions. The negatives automatically inject themselves into thought impulses, ensuring passage into the subconscious. The positives must be injected through autosuggestion. These emotions may be likened to yeast in bread—they constitute the ACTION element transforming thought impulses from passive to active state.
220: Hill explains that one is preparing to influence and control the 'inner audience' of the subconscious mind to hand over the DESIRE for money. It is essential to understand the method of approach—speaking the language of emotion or feeling. He presents 'The Seven Major Positive Emotions': the emotion of DESIRE, the emotion of FAITH, the emotion of LOVE, the emotion of SEX, the emotion of ENTHUSIASM, the emotion of ROMANCE, and the emotion of HOPE. There are other positive emotions, but these are the seven most powerful and most commonly used in creative effort. Master these seven (only by USE), and other positive emotions will be at your command. One does not become money-conscious by filling the mind with negative emotions. He then begins presenting 'The Seven Major Negative Emotions (To be avoided)': the emotion of FEAR, the emotion of JEALOUSY, the emotion of HATRED, the emotion of REVENGE—and continues onto the next page.
